newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING Barings urge neutral stance in Hungary shares.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings urge neutral stance in Hungary shares.

text.p: ING Barings suggested investors should take a neutral stance in Hungarian stocks in the next three months relative to other markets in the region.

"Given concerns about the need for a short-term correction, we recommend a broadly neutral weighting through to the end of the first quarter of 1997," ING Barings' analysts said in a December publication on east European asset allocation.

The Budapest Stock Exchange has risen more than 100 percent in dollar terms this year, substantially outperforming emerging markets and other east European market with the exception of Russia, they said.

ING Barings chose food, beverages and construction as sector favourites, in addition to firm holdings in drugs, chemicals and plastics stocks, and suggested reducing stakes in the banking sector and slightly raising in the energy sector buys.

"Within a broadly neutral stance relative to the rest of the region, from a sectoral bias we favour food and beverages (Pick and Sopron ) and construction (Zalakeramia ) with core holdings in pharmaceuticals, chemicals and plastics," ING Barings said.

"We recommend an underweight position in banking, a sector which will suffer from sluggish GDP growth and growing competition, and we are also slightly underweight in energy stocks, despite our forecast for a rebound in earnings from MOL."
Currently the stocks of only two banks, OTP and Inter-Europa Bank, are listed on the Budapest bourse.
